description: Converge session listing to a single canonical panel with status/stage filtering, createdAt/tokens/duration sorting, responsive row layout, and add prev/next + sibling-sidebar navigation on the session page.

tasks.title: Remove dead session-list trio and converge to canonical panel
tasks.description: Delete the dead stub `SessionDetail.tsx`, the unused `SessionList.tsx`, and their sole consumer `SessionHeader.tsx` along with their test files, and remove the `SessionList` export from the `widgets/coder-session/index.ts` barrel. After removal, `WorkflowSessionsPanel` is the single canonical session-list component rendered by `IssueDetailPage`.
acceptanceCriteria: `packages/web/src/widgets/coder-session/ui/SessionDetail.tsx`, `SessionList.tsx`, and `SessionHeader.tsx` are deleted
Their corresponding test files are deleted
`SessionList` is no longer exported from `widgets/coder-session/index.ts`
Grep across `packages/web/src` finds zero remaining imports of `SessionDetail`, `SessionList`, or `SessionHeader`
`IssueDetailPage` still renders `WorkflowSessionsPanel` as the sole session list
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes with no dangling references
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes
tasks.output: Deleted files + cleaned barrel export; green typecheck and test run
tasks.notes: Grep already confirms zero external consumers. `formatDuration` in SessionHeader is duplicated in SessionPage, so deletion breaks no shared dependency.

tasks.title: Add status/stage filtering and createdAt/tokens/duration sorting to WorkflowSessionsPanel
tasks.description: Create a `useWorkflowSessionFiltering` hook (in `widgets/issue-workflow/model/`) owning `statusFilter`, `stageFilter`, and `sortKey` state plus a `useMemo` that filters then sorts `WorkflowRunSession[]`. Add a compact control row above the session list in `WorkflowSessionsPanel` with a status filter (All + running/completed/failed + present statuses), a stage filter (plan/build/check/integrate), and a sort select (createdAt default / tokens / duration). Filters combine with AND; default sort is createdAt ascending.
acceptanceCriteria: `useWorkflowSessionFiltering` hook is unit-tested in isolation (no rendering) covering: filter by status, filter by stage, combined status+stage filters, clearing one filter keeps the other active, default sort is createdAt ascending, sort by tokens, sort by duration, and sort applies only to filtered rows
Status filter options include at least `running`, `completed`, and `failed`
Stage filter options include `plan`, `build`, `check`, and `integrate`
Selecting status `failed` hides non-failed sessions; selecting stage `build` hides non-build sessions
Default sort (no selection) renders sessions ordered by createdAt ascending
Duration sort measures completed sessions to completion time and live sessions to current time
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes
tasks.output: useWorkflowSessionFiltering hook + filter/sort control row wired into WorkflowSessionsPanel + unit tests
tasks.notes: Token fallback: usage.totalTokens, else inputTokens + outputTokens, else 0. Duration logic mirrors SessionPage.tsx:272-276. Filtering/sorting are pure client-side view computations over data already fetched by useWorkflowRunSessions.

tasks.title: Make WorkflowSessionRow responsive on narrow containers
tasks.description: Tighten the `WorkflowSessionRow` CSS so content wraps gracefully instead of overflowing on narrow viewports: add `min-w-0` to the outer container and inner flex children, ensure the name+status line wraps (session name truncates, model badge wraps to a second visual line), and verify no fixed-width element forces horizontal scroll.
acceptanceCriteria: Session row content wraps across multiple lines on a narrow container width rather than staying on a single non-wrapping line
Session name and status remain visible and legible at narrow widths
The workflow sessions panel produces no horizontal overflow on narrow viewports
Metric chips wrap gracefully instead of being truncated out of view
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes
tasks.output: Responsive WorkflowSessionRow layout with min-w-0 + flex-wrap + truncate constraints
tasks.notes: The existing two-line layout already has flex-wrap on the metrics line; this task tightens constraints (min-w-0, truncate) rather than restructuring.

tasks.title: Add prev/next sibling navigation and sibling-sessions sidebar to SessionPage
tasks.description: On `SessionPage`, add a `useWorkflowRunSessions(issue?.workflowRunId)` call (issue already fetched via `useIssue`) to obtain the canonical sibling set. Compute siblings sorted by createdAt ascending, locate the current session by sessionName, and render prev/next navigation (disabled/hidden at boundaries) as react-router Links to the sibling transcript path. Add a sibling-sessions sidebar (visible on `xl:`+ viewports, hidden on narrow) listing siblings as navigable entries with the current session highlighted.
acceptanceCriteria: Prev/next navigation follows the canonical createdAt-ascending sibling ordering
"Previous session" is disabled or hidden when viewing the first sibling; "next session" is disabled or hidden when viewing the last sibling
Prev/next navigation stays within the current issue's session set
Sidebar lists sibling sessions as navigable entries; activating an entry navigates to that session
Sidebar visually indicates the currently viewed session
Sidebar session set matches the WorkflowSessionsPanel set for the same workflow run (both read from useWorkflowRunSessions)
Sidebar appears on wide viewports (xl:) and is hidden on narrow viewports, while prev/next buttons remain always visible
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes
tasks.output: Prev/next nav controls + sibling sidebar on SessionPage + tests
tasks.notes: The existing useCoderSessions call stays for current-session lookup; useWorkflowRunSessions is added for sibling parity with the panel. Match current session by sessionName (route identifier), fall back gracefully.
